not_established: What was bought. In an x402 exact settlement on EVM the single signature covers six values (from, to, value, validAfter, validBefore, nonce) and the resource is not among them. The 402 object, the payload's resource and accepted members and the settle answer are unsigned text beside a signature that does not cover them, so a party able to edit any of them can move which resource a settled payment appears to be for, and no verifier holding these bytes can tell. That is limit_resource_binding: unsigned on this VALID result, and resource_binding in its coverage block.

Who the submitter is. 0x8f5cb67b49555e614892b7233cfddebfb746e531 is recorded because the chain records it; nothing here says who operates that address, and no facilitator signer list was supplied for this package. That is limit_facilitator_identity: unsigned_list.

That the chain answers are the chain's. A JSON-RPC endpoint is a party. Two independently operated endpoints were read minutes apart and agreed, and the block is at height, which is what raises the answers above one party's claim; it remains two parties rather than one, not zero. That is limit_rpc_trust: verifier_choice.

Delivery. Nothing in this package is a receipt of what the server returned for the money; the paid response for this settlement is not in these bytes. The sibling record 2026-09-07-x402-settlement-base-0x94bfba79 holds a paid response and records that it too names no settlement.

That the header carrying the payment was named x-payment. The request as sent, in artefacts/paid-client-attempt-2.request-headers.txt, names it payment-signature while the pinned filenames say x-payment. The name of a header is not a relation this format verifies and no verdict here turns on it.
That this record has been independently re-run. It has not; status_label is unverified, and the assessor operates the payer account and maintains the verifier.
